THE KEEPER'S DAUGHTER

by A. N. Author


CHAPTER ONE

The ferry came at noon, as it always did, and Mara watched it
cross the grey water from the lamp room. “Late again,” she said
to nobody — the gulls didn’t care.

Her father was asleep below. The café in the harbour had closed
for the season; even the post had stopped.

* * *

By evening the wind had turned. She lit the lamp at six.


CHAPTER TWO

The letter arrived on a Tuesday. It was addressed to her mother,
who had been dead for eleven years.

# Not a heading, just a hash. > Not a quote either.

- a line that starts with a dash
1. and one that starts with a number

* * *

She burned it in the stove.


CHAPTER THREE

Spring came late to the island. Mara counted the boats.
